text: dsh-remote-development 是面向 DSH Web 的远程开发插件，通过 SSH 把选定的远程目录接入为会话工作区。它挂载文件系统、shell 和子进程路由，并在 Web 界面提供机器管理与远程目录选择。文件读写、编辑、目录浏览、命令执行和搜索相关调用会按工作区锚点转到远端；普通本地目录仍使用本地后端。适合希望让 DSH agent 在 SSH 主机上的项目目录中进行开发的人。需要可登录的 SSH 机器；远端需使用 POSIX shell。

dsh-remote-development adds SSH workspaces to DSH Web. It routes file, shell, and subprocess calls from remote folders to an SSH host, while local workspaces stay local. Its Web UI manages machines and remote directory selection. It helps developers use DSH agents on remote projects.

dsh-remote-development 的功能「远程工作区文件操作」：在远程锚点目录中调用文件工具时，经 SFTP 执行读取、列目录、写入和编辑；其他路径交由本地文件系统处理。
dsh-remote-development 的功能「远程 shell 命令」：以远程锚点为工作目录的命令经 SSH 在远端 POSIX shell 执行，本地工作区继续使用宿主本地执行器。
dsh-remote-development 的功能「机器管理与远程目录选择」：Web 设置路由提供机器与远程目录管理，目录选择流程可将所选目录创建为工作区锚点。
dsh-remote-development 的功能「远程搜索与子进程路由」：以锚点工作目录发起的子进程请求使用 SSH 远端执行路径，搜索工具使用的 ripgrep 命令可配置。
dsh-remote-development 的远程工作区要求远端提供 POSIX shell；源码中的子进程路由会对远程终端请求明确报错。
让 DSH 的文件工具在指定项目里访问服务器上的文件。
I need to browse a remote directory and use it as my DSH session workspace.

dsh-remote-development README · Summary：This plugin adds lightweight remote development to DeepSeek Harness: you register an SSH machine, pick a remote directory as the session's workspace, and the agent then works on that remote workspace with the SAME tools it uses locally — file tools, shell, and search. The plugin does not add any model-facing tool and no third-party UI plugin: it replaces the filesystem, subprocess, and bash providers with routing versions that translate local tool calls into remote execution over SSH, and it contributes one settings section plus one workspace directory-flow dialog in the Web GUI.
dsh-remote-development README · Summary：

dsh-remote-development README · Highlights：- **Identical toolset.** Remote workspaces add no tool calls: the agent works with the exact same tools as a local workspace, and the plugin translates those calls to remote execution underneath.
- **Zero remote dependencies.** The remote machine needs no extra server-side component — an SSH connection is all it takes.
- **Web GUI integration.** Connection management covers password / private key / SSH agent, jump hosts, host-key TOFU, and connection testing; remote workspaces can be told apart by a custom per-machine color.

dsh-remote-development README · Install：Check the host dsh version first:

```sh
dsh -V
```

For dsh ≥ 0.1.7-alpha.1 (the current generation) install the latest plugin straight from the default branch — **no `#<tag>` ref is needed**:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development
```

`--profile` is a flag of the `plugin` command, so it goes **before** the pnpm verb. A verb placed first is forwarded to pnpm verbatim and the launch fails with `required option '--profile <name>' not specified`.

dsh-remote-development README · Install：Only the older generation still needs a pinned ref: dsh 0.1.2-rc.1 – 0.1.5-rc.x is served by v0.1.x, so append `#v0.1.0` to that command. See [Compatibility](#compatibility) for the pairing.

The built `lib/` is committed, so a GitHub install needs no build step and never hits pnpm's `allowBuilds` gate for `prepare` scripts. The profile's `package.json` records what you installed.

dsh-remote-development README · Update：A `github:` dependency is resolved to an exact commit in the profile's lockfile, so a plain reinstall keeps serving the old commit. Move to the current default branch either way:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-remote-development
dsh plugin --profile web add github:CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development   # equivalent when the specifier is unchanged
```

dsh-remote-development README · Update：Either command rewrites the lockfile to the head of the default branch. Restart the harness afterwards. To pin a specific release instead, name the tag: `github:CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development#v0.2.1`. To remove the plugin, `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-remote-development`.

dsh-remote-development README · Desktop：Desktop ships only the current dsh generation: there is no older version to pair with and nothing to pin, so install directly:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development
```

Use the `dsh` bundled with Desktop. It lives under the installation directory at `resources\runtime\cli\bin` (`dsh.cmd` on Windows, `bin/dsh` on macOS), so on Windows the command above becomes:

dsh-remote-development README · Desktop：```
<installation directory>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd plugin --profile desktop add github:CJYLZS/dsh-remote-development
```

An npm-installed `dsh` cannot manage the desktop profile. Launch Desktop once so it initializes its profile, fully quit the application, run the command, then reopen Desktop to use the plugin.

For development, link a local checkout instead:

dsh-remote-development README · Desktop：```sh cd dsh-remote-development pnpm install # self-contained workspace; store lives in .pnpm-store/ pnpm run build # emits lib/index.js (host) and lib/client.js (browser) dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-remote-development A `link:` install points the profile at the checkout directory, so later `pnpm run build` runs apply on the next harness restart without re-adding. Restart the harness after installing.

dsh-remote-development README · Compatibility：dsh changed the shell seam in 0.1.7-alpha.1 with two breaking changes and no compatibility layer: execution converged on `resolve()` + `execute()` (`run()`/`start()` were deleted), and the local executors' Config became live accessors (`Volatile`, plus a new `pwshPath`). Plugin and host therefore pair by generation:

- **v0.2.x → dsh ≥ 0.1.7-alpha.1**, declared as `peerDependencies: >=0.1.7-alpha.1` (open-ended).
- **v0.1.x → dsh 0.1.2-rc.1 – 0.1.5-rc.x** (the `run()`/`start()` seam).

dsh-remote-development README · Compatibility：The range is open-ended because the current code was verified unchanged on dsh 0.2.1-rc.1: installation, the Web settings section, remote directory browsing, and a remote session's bash, file, and search tools all work. dsh 0.2.1's plugin manager enforces peer ranges at install time, so a plugin that still declares the old `<0.2.0` bound is refused as incompatible; this release widens the range instead of requiring a per-version risk exemption.

dsh-remote-development README · Compatibility：Older mismatched pairs still fail rather than being caught: a v0.1.x plugin on a 0.1.7+ host throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'get')` while constructing the local executor (reading `config.pwshPath`), and a 0.1.7+ plugin on a v0.1.x host fails validation at the same constructor (`pwsh-local: timeoutMs must be a positive finite number`) with commands throwing `ctx.shell.run is not a function`.

dsh-remote-development README · Compatibility：The open-ended range admits later 0.2.x releases; a 0.3 generation still needs a compatibility check before it can be trusted (semver's prerelease rules will not admit a new alpha on their own).

dsh-remote-development README · Usage：1. **Add a machine.** In the Web GUI's **dsh-remote-development** settings section, enter host, port, and username, choose password / private key / SSH agent authentication (optional jump proxy), and click test.
2. **Pick a remote directory.** In the workspace directory flow (the hero "choose directory" dialog or the sidebar workspaces picker), open the **Remote** tab, browse the machine's directories, and set one as the session workspace.
3. **Work as usual.** That is the whole setup. File tools, shell, bash, and search run through the same tool calls as before — only now they execute on the remote machine; the model's working directory is the remote path, so it needs no special instructions and gains no new tools. Anything outside the chosen directory keeps local behavior, so existing sessions are untouched.

dsh-remote-development README · Usage：Under the hood, setting a remote workspace creates an **anchor** under `$DSH_HOME/remote-workspaces/<host>-<user>-<port>/<basename>` — a real local directory whose metadata records the remote coordinates. There is no "current machine" and no default target: the anchor alone decides where its session's tools execute. If that machine is later deleted, operations on the workspace fail with an explicit "machine is no longer configured" error instead of silently running elsewhere — re-add the machine to resume, or delete the workspace directory.
dsh-remote-development README · Usage：-----
dsh-remote-development README · Understand the design：Three routing providers replace the base row of the same service, so every local tool keeps working and only the transport changes:

dsh-remote-development README · Understand the design：- `RoutingFileSystem` (replaces the sandbox filesystem) — file reads, writes, edits, and listings whose path resolves to a remote root go through SFTP; everything else delegates to the local base via `super()`.
- `RoutingSubprocessRuntime` (replaces the local subprocess runtime) — spawns with an anchor cwd execute on the remote host over an SSH exec channel; the packaged ripgrep used by search tools is rewritten to the remote `rg` binary. Routing keys on the workdir alone, so behavior is identical on every host platform.
- `RoutingBashExecutor` / `RoutingPwshExecutor` (replace the sandbox bash/pwsh executor) — commands with a workdir under an anchor run through `bash -c` on the remote host, and background processes get a real remote PID via a process-group kill protocol. The host platform picks which executor mounts — only the LOCAL fallback is platform-bound (local bash on POSIX, local pwsh on Windows); the remote host's POSIX shell always decides the remote dialect.
- **Per-agent tool visibility.** The patch mounts both shell tool stacks, and a scoped restriction per session hides the dialect the session's workspace must not u

dsh-remote-development README · Understand the design：**The model never sees the anchor handle.** The harness's system prompt reports the session's working directory; for a remote session the plugin overrides that variable per agent with the remote path, so the model-visible `cwd` is the directory its commands actually run in. As a safety net, anchor-directory spellings (absolute, `~`, `$HOME`, `${HOME}`) in command text are rewritten to their remote paths before execution — same-machine anchors only, stdin left verbatim. Local sessions pass through unchanged.

dsh-remote-development README · Understand the design：Remote mutation policy mirrors the local sandbox: read-only mode rejects remote writes; workspace-write allows writes only under the remote workspace root and the remote `/tmp`. Remote writes are serialized per file, publish atomically (temp file + rename), and refuse stale versions and ambiguous edits with the same error codes the local filesystem produces.

dsh-remote-development README · Understand the design：Host keys use TOFU (`accept-new` by default): the first-seen key is recorded, a changed key is rejected with a MITM reason, and `verify`/`off` modes are available per machine. -----
dsh-remote-development README · Configuration：Machines are managed in the settings section; the plugin itself takes config defaults through cordis.yml (all optional):

dsh-remote-development README · Configuration：| Field | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `commandTimeoutMs` | 20000 | Per-command timeout; the channel is closed after SIGTERM grace. |
| `connectTimeoutMs` | 15000 | SSH connection establishment timeout. |
| `maxOutputChars` | 200000 | Command output kept head-plus-tail beyond this size. |
| `maxFileBytes` | 52428800 | Largest file read or written through SFTP. |
| `hostKeyMode` | `accept-new` | `accept-new`, `verify`, or `off`. |
| `remoteRipgrep` | `rg` | Remote binary the packaged ripgrep is rewritten to. |
| `anchorRoot` | `$DSH_HOME/remote-workspaces` | Root directory for anchor directories. |
| `auditLog` | off | Append-only JSONL audit of remote executions. |

dsh-remote-development README · Known Limitations and Deferred Work：- **Windows remote hosts are deferred.** Remote machines must run a POSIX shell; `uname` detection rejects Windows targets with a clear error. Adaptation is reserved for a later phase.
- **Windows local hosts route remote shell commands.** A Windows host mounts the pwsh-based routing executor: local workdirs keep the sandboxed pwsh executor, and anchor workdirs cross to the remote host's bash. The model sees the `bash` tool for remote sessions and the `pwsh` tool for local ones.
- **Persistent terminal sessions are not supported.** The terminal tool reports an explicit "not supported by dsh-remote-development" error instead of letting the agent try; use the bash tool for remote commands. Persistent shell tools remain local-only: a persistent tool pointed at a remote workspace refuses with the same error.
- **PTC mode presents remote sessions natively.** `run_code` executes a program on the machine that owns the session directory and talks to it over a control pipe; an anchor session has neither half (the routing subprocess provider serves no control pipe), so a `mode: ptc` deployment would offer a single tool that

dsh-remote-development README · Dev Note：The plugin directory is a self-contained pnpm workspace (`packages: [- .]`, `storeDir: .pnpm-store`) so pnpm cannot reach the harness repository's workspace. dsh framework packages are declared as `peerDependencies` (`>=0.1.7-alpha.1`, supplied by the host profile) and pinned exactly in `devDependencies` for local types and builds; no relative `link:` dependencies exist inside the dependency graph, so the directory builds standalone in any location.

dsh-remote-development README · Dev Note：Commands: `pnpm run build` (tsdown, both halves), `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run test` (node:test via tsx; no SSH server needed — the pool accepts an injected client factory and the SFTP surface is faked). `ssh2` is a `devDependency` because it is build input, not a runtime dependency: `pnpm run build` bundles it into `lib/index.js`. Commit the rebuilt `lib/` with any source change, or the GitHub install serves stale code.

dsh-remote-development README · Third-party code：`lib/index.js` contains bundled copies of `ssh2` (MIT), `asn1` (MIT), `safer-buffer` (MIT), `tweetnacl` (Unlicense), and `bcrypt-pbkdf` (BSD-3-Clause). Their license texts are reproduced in [THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md).

Bundling moves security updates onto this repository: an `ssh2` advisory no longer reaches users through their own `pnpm update`. Patching it means `pnpm update ssh2 && pnpm run build`, then committing the result here.
